hypotheses.title: Coordinate prefill admission within an active expert-parallel collective group
hypotheses.mechanism: Proposed, untested adaptation of deadline-aware chunking: each rank retains local request ownership, while ranks that must enter the same MoE collective agree on an iteration-level prefill limit using the slowest predicted participating rank. A collective group is determined from the resolved backend and process groups, not assumed to equal all eight GPUs. Independent replicas make separate decisions.
hypotheses.nearest_prior_art: SLOWeave supplies the deadline-based chunk rule; P-PAS supplies online token-budget adaptation; FlowPrefill addresses the scheduling-granularity tradeoff. The earlier B200 shortlist supplies a fixed cadence proposal.
hypotheses.new_adaptation: The candidate addition is a group-scoped admission contract that accounts for rank skew, collective participation, supported graph shapes, and KV capacity. Whether the historical pinned runtime already has equivalent behavior is unverified.
hypotheses.code_surface: After resolving the active backend: scheduler admission and token budgeting, per-rank deadline and timing summaries, process-group coordination, graph-shape checks, KV reservation, and stale-state fallback.
hypotheses.online_policy: Observe each participating rank's active decode deadlines, queued prefill tokens, graph-compatible token capacities, free KV blocks, and recent iteration and collective-wait times. Calibrate a conservative per-shape cost estimate from recent complete iterations and include coordination time. At each group iteration, choose the largest shared prefill limit for which the predicted slowest-rank finish precedes the earliest reported decode deadline; ranks admit local chunks within that limit. Share the decision only among ranks required by the resolved collective. If no chunk fits, run decode-only when feasible. If a deadline is already overdue, prioritize decode and record the miss; when no decode is active, admit bounded prefill subject to graph and KV limits. Bound prefill waiting with an explicit age threshold, accepting and recording a deadline tradeoff if progress requires it. Control messages, prediction, and extra small iterations add overhead. On stale timing, coordination failure, unsupported shape, or insufficient KV, use the best qualified fixed cadence and budget. Strongest static comparator: a matched fixed cadence and token-budget sweep.
hypotheses.strongest_objection: SLOWeave already establishes the central deadline rule. The supplied collective code applies specifically to passthrough all-to-all experts, and the pinned active backend is unknown. Target traces may show little mixed-step rank skew; coordination and smaller chunks could then lose to fixed settings.

novelty.deployment: Unestablished for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on B200 in either DEP8 or two DEP4 replicas.
novelty.implementation: A collective-scoped scheduling contract is proposed; its absence from the pinned runtime is unproved.
novelty.publication: Unestablished because deadline-aware and adaptive-budget scheduling are close prior art.

hypotheses.confidence: Moderate mechanism plausibility; low confidence in target benefit or implementation novelty.
hypotheses.readiness: Trace gate only. Resolve the historical backend and process groups, then require mixed prefill/decode iterations with material rank skew before implementation.

rubric.value: Possible TPOT-tail protection during mixed prefill and decode; TTFT, throughput, and cost may worsen. No target gain is established.
rubric.mechanism: Local admission under a shared limit for ranks that actually share an active collective.
rubric.evidence: Prior-art abstracts and a branch diff motivate a trace-gated test; neither establishes measured transfer.
rubric.integration: High until the pinned backend, process groups, graph repertoire, and scheduler contract are resolved.
rubric.correctness: Preserve per-request token order, collective participation where required, graph and KV bounds, and output agreement at matched precision and sampling.
rubric.experiment: Trace incidence and skew first; compare unchanged pin, tuned fixed settings, and an applicable SLOWeave-style controller.
rubric.cost: Read-only trace analysis and CPU replay precede any implementation or GPU serving experiment; later cost is unknown.
rubric.distinctness: Potentially distinct group coordination; deadline selection and adaptive budgeting themselves are established ideas.
rubric.research_contribution: Conditional implementation adaptation; publication novelty unestablished.

experiment.control: Independently qualify DEP8 and two DEP4 replicas. At matched model, backend, precision, MTP/DSpark state, graph repertoire, KV capacity, cache preparation, request bodies, and concurrency, compare unchanged pinned behavior, a fixed cadence and budget sweep, and an applicable SLOWeave-style controller. Include the refreshed guide's DEP4 cadence only at applicable load and configuration.
experiment.treatment: The proposed collective-group policy with the same graph and memory limits.
experiment.measurements: Mixed-step incidence, per-rank work and collective wait, predictor error, decision overhead, graph choices, queue age, cache misses, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, cost per token, peak memory, and answer quality for the approximately 8K-input/1K-output agent workload across loads.
experiment.reject_if: The required skew pattern is immaterial, no reliable group contract exists on the active backend, prediction or coordination consumes the available slack, prefill starves, or the best matched comparator meets or beats the treatment on required service and quality criteria.
experiment.correctness: Check unequal and empty rank batches under the active collective path, cancellation, cache hits and misses, graph replay, KV exhaustion, and output agreement at matched precision and sampling.
experiment.cost: Trace and CPU replay first; build, capture, serving time, and memory overhead remain unknown.

hypotheses.revision_after_critique: Retained as a single trace-gated adaptation. The group is the resolved collective's participating ranks; independent replicas do not wait on one another. The policy now defines predictor calibration, overdue and no-fitting-chunk behavior, graph and KV limits, and stale-state fallback.
